questions.prompt: The manifestations of a disease are best defined as the
options: subjective feelings of discomfort during a chronic illness.
signs and symptoms of a disease
factors that precipitate an acute episode of a chronic illness.
early indicators of the prodromal stage of infection.
questions.suggestedLabel: B. signs and symptoms of a disease
questions.suggestedRationale: Manifestations are the signs and symptoms of a disease.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be the most likely cause of an iatrogenic disease?
options: A combination of specific etiological factors
An unwanted effect of a prescribed drug
Prolonged exposure to toxic chemicals in the environment
questions.suggestedLabel: C. An unwanted effect of a prescribed drug
questions.suggestedRationale: Iatrogenic disease is caused by a treatment or prescribed drug.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered a systemic sign of disease?
questions.suggestedRationale: Fever is a systemic sign; the other options are localized findings.

questions.prompt: A type of cellular adaptation in which there is a decrease in cell size is referred to as
questions.suggestedRationale: Atrophy is a decrease in cell size.

questions.prompt: A change in a tissue marked by cells that vary in size and shape and show increased mitotic figures would be called
questions.suggestedRationale: Dysplasia is disordered growth with variable cell size/shape and increased mitoses.

questions.prompt: A deficit of oxygen in the cells usually due to respiratory or circulatory problems is called
questions.suggestedRationale: Among these options, ischemia is the oxygen deficit in cells from circulatory (or related) compromise; hypoxia is not listed.

questions.prompt: When a group of cells in the body dies, the change is called
questions.suggestedRationale: Necrosis is death of a group of cells in the body.

questions.prompt: The term cancer refers to
questions.suggestedRationale: Cancer refers to a malignant neoplasm.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
options: Alteration of DNA does not change cell function.
Damaged cells may be able to repair themselves
All types of cells die at the same rate.
Mild ischemia causes immediate cell death.
questions.suggestedLabel: B. Damaged cells may be able to repair themselves
questions.suggestedRationale: Mildly injured cells can often repair themselves if the stressor is removed.

questions.prompt: Caseation necrosis refers to an area where
options: dead cells form a thick cheesy substance
questions.suggestedLabel: C. dead cells form a thick cheesy substance
questions.suggestedRationale: Caseous necrosis is a thick, cheesy debris typical of TB lesions.

questions.prompt: A circumstance that causes a sudden acute episode of a chronic disease to occur is termed
questions.suggestedRationale: A precipitating factor triggers an acute flare of a chronic disease.

questions.prompt: Routine application of sun block to skin and vaccination would be an example of
questions.suggestedRationale: Sunscreen and vaccines are preventive measures.

questions.prompt: Which term is used to describe a new and secondary or additional problem that arises after the original disease has been established?
questions.suggestedRationale: A complication is a new secondary problem after the original disease.

questions.prompt: Which of the following can cause cell injury or death?
questions.suggestedRationale: Hypoxia, extreme cold, pressure, and chemical toxins can all injure or kill cells.

questions.prompt: A collection of signs and symptoms, often affecting more than one organ or system, that usually occur together in response to a certain condition is referred to as a(an)
questions.suggestedRationale: A syndrome is a set of signs and symptoms that occur together.

questions.prompt: All of the following statements are correct about cell damage EXCEPT:
options: The initial stage of cell damage often causes an alteration in metabolic reactions.
If the factor causing the damage is removed quickly, the cell may be able to recover and return to its normal state.
If the noxious factor remains for an extended period of time, the damage becomes irreversible and the cell dies.
Initially, cell damage does not change cell metabolism, structure, or function
questions.suggestedLabel: D. Initially, cell damage does not change cell metabolism, structure, or function
questions.suggestedRationale: The false statement is that early cell injury leaves metabolism, structure, and function unchanged.

questions.prompt: If the data collected from the research process confirm that the new treatment has increased effectiveness and is safe, this is called
questions.suggestedRationale: Confirmed safety and effectiveness from research is evidence-based research.

questions.prompt: When prolonged ischemia occurs to an area of the heart, the resulting damage is referred to as
questions.suggestedRationale: Prolonged myocardial ischemia produces infarction.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is usually included in a medical history?
questions.suggestedRationale: A complete history includes past and current illness, prescribed and OTC drugs, and allergies.

questions.prompt: A therapy that has been approved for use and may show additional potential to treat a different disease is termed “_____” use.
questions.suggestedRationale: Approved drugs used for an unapproved indication are off-label use.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct proportion of water to body weight to be expected in a healthy male adult’s body:
questions.suggestedRationale: A healthy adult male is about 60% body water.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct proportion of blood (to body weight) in an adult male’s body: 30%
questions.suggestedRationale: Blood is about 4% of adult male body weight in standard patho tables; the '30%' in the stem looks like a typo.

questions.prompt: The osmoreceptor cells controlling the thirst mechanism are located in the
questions.suggestedRationale: Osmoreceptors that drive thirst are in the hypothalamus.

questions.prompt: When the osmotic pressure of the blood is elevated above normal, water would shift from the
questions.suggestedLabel: C. interstitial compartment into the blood
questions.suggestedRationale: High blood osmotic pressure pulls water from the interstitial fluid into the vascular space.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would result from a deficit of plasma proteins?
questions.suggestedRationale: Low plasma proteins lower plasma oncotic pressure, so fluid leaves the vessels.

questions.prompt: Which of the following would likely be related to an elevated hematocrit reading?
questions.suggestedRationale: Dehydration concentrates red cells and raises hematocrit.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a typical sign of dehydration?
questions.suggestedRationale: Dry, rough oral mucosa is a typical sign of dehydration.

questions.prompt: Excessive Sweating is a common cause for?
questions.suggestedRationale: Textbooks list excessive sweating as a common cause of hyponatremia from sodium loss in sweat (hypercalcemia is unrelated).

questions.prompt: Primary Cation in the ECF is Sodium and Potassium in ICF. True or False
questions.suggestedRationale: Sodium is the main ECF cation and potassium is the main ICF cation.

questions.prompt: Which of the following results from hypocalcemia?
questions.suggestedRationale: Hypocalcemia increases skeletal-muscle twitching/spasms and weakens cardiac contraction; constipation and low phosphate fit hypercalcemia.

questions.prompt: Which of the following causes tetany?
questions.suggestedRationale: Tetany is caused by low serum calcium (increased neuromuscular irritability).

questions.prompt: Phosphate Ion plays a major role in all of the following except
questions.suggestedRationale: Phosphate is important in bone and acid-base balance and relates inversely to calcium; it is not a major clotting factor (calcium is).

questions.prompt: Alkalosis increases irritability and spontaneous stimulation of nerves by
options: increasing the permeability of nerve membranes
questions.suggestedLabel: B. increasing the permeability of nerve membranes
questions.suggestedRationale: Alkalosis increases nerve-membrane permeability and excitability.

questions.prompt: What system controls the bicarbonate and carbonic acid buffer system
questions.suggestedRationale: The carbonic acid–bicarbonate buffer is controlled by the lungs (CO2) and kidneys (HCO3−).

questions.prompt: Serum potassium levels are affected by
questions.suggestedRationale: Aldosterone, hydrogen-ion concentration, and insulin all shift or excrete potassium; ADH does not primarily regulate K+.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the primary control of serum Na+ levels?
questions.suggestedRationale: Aldosterone is the primary hormonal control of body sodium (ADH mainly controls water).

questions.prompt: Which of the following results from hypocalcemia?
questions.suggestedRationale: Same as the earlier hypocalcemia item: muscle spasms plus weak cardiac contractions.

questions.prompt: Which system is the slowest to have an impact on acid base balance?
questions.suggestedRationale: Renal compensation is the slowest acid-base control system.

questions.prompt: What is the effect on blood serum when excessive lactic acid accumulates in the body?
questions.suggestedRationale: Lactic acid is buffered by bicarbonate, so serum HCO3− falls (metabolic acidosis, lower pH).

questions.prompt: The direct effects of acidosis are manifested primarily in the functioning of the?
questions.suggestedRationale: Acidosis primarily depresses the central nervous system.

questions.prompt: patients with impaired expiration associated with emphysema, effective compensation for the acid-base imbalance would be
options: increased rate and depth of respiration.
decreased rate and depth of respiration.
increased urine pH and decreased serum bicarbonate.
decreased urine pH and increased serum bicarbonate.
questions.suggestedLabel: D. decreased urine pH and increased serum bicarbonate.
questions.suggestedRationale: Emphysema causes CO2 retention (respiratory acidosis); kidneys compensate by retaining bicarbonate and excreting acid (lower urine pH).

questions.prompt: A prolonged state of metabolic acidosis often leads to
questions.suggestedRationale: In acidosis, H+ enters cells in exchange for K+, raising serum potassium.

questions.prompt: Place the following events in the correct sequence of events when ketoacids increase in the blood of a diabetic patient. Not all options are used in the answers.
questions.suggestedRationale: Ketoacids consume HCO3− and lower pH, then Kussmaul respirations drop PCO2, urine acidifies, and pH begins to recover.

questions.prompt: Which statements apply to atrial natriuretic peptide?
options: It is secreted by heart muscle cells.
It is a hormone secreted by the kidneys.
It helps to control water and sodium balance.
It is released in response to low blood pressure.
questions.suggestedRationale: ANP is released by stretched cardiac muscle and promotes sodium and water loss; it is not a renal hormone and is not triggered by low blood pressure.

questions.prompt: Increased milk and/or antacid intake can contribute to development of “milk-alkali syndrome,” which can cause which of the following?
During the stress response, endorphins act as
options: stimulators of increased secretion of aldosterone and insulin.
an enhancer of the immune response.
questions.suggestedRationale: Endorphins released in the stress response act as natural pain blockers.

questions.prompt: Severe, prolonged stress may cause acute renal failure or stress ulcers to develop as a result of
options: a deficit of glucose and oxygen in the body.
the supply of hormones having been exhausted.
questions.suggestedRationale: Prolonged stress vasoconstriction can ischemicize the gut and kidney, leading to stress ulcers or acute renal failure.

questions.prompt: The stress response involves the integrated action of the
questions.suggestedRationale: The stress response integrates hypothalamus, pituitary (hypophysis), sympathetic nerves, and adrenal glands.

questions.prompt: Which of the following may alter a person’s perception of a stressor?
options: A: The presence of several stressors at the same time
C: Lack of effective coping mechanisms
questions.suggestedRationale: Multiple simultaneous stressors, past experience, and poor coping all change how a stressor is perceived.
